assessments.reasoning: I independently retrieved and verified the exact bytes of System Programming in a High Level Language and inspected the cited passage (A §2.1, The Algol68C Project, printed pp. 7–8 (physical PDF pp. 11–12)). Birrell’s §2.1 on printed pages 7–8 starts with the Cambridge Algol68C compiling system growing out of Bourne and Guy’s experimental system written in 1970. It identifies that system’s Z70 language and the new portable compiler decision.

challenge.method: Separate the Z70 language, its Titan system, the Algol68C language usage on printed page 8, and the portable compiler described in the same section.
challenge.results: The name has both language and compiler uses in Birrell. The candidate’s express compiling-system scope identifies the implementation and keeps the source-language referent separate.

limitations: The identity concerns the Cambridge compiling system and its documented origins. It gives no semantic inventory for the accepted language.
